issues.legal_issue: A child of a marriage that is void under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act is statutorily legitimate regardless of when the child was born or whether a decree of nullity was granted.
A child conceived or begotten before a decree annulling a voidable marriage is deemed legitimate if the child would have been legitimate had the marriage been dissolved rather than annulled.
A child whose legitimacy is conferred under Section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act has rights in or to the property of the parents, but not the property of any other person.
A child whose legitimacy is conferred under Section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act does not thereby become a Mitakshara coparcener or acquire coparcenary rights by birth.

A child whose legitimacy is conferred under Section 16 is entitled to a share in the property allotted to a parent upon the notional partition required by Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act, where the parent dies intestate.
Legitimacy conferred under Section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act must be recognized when determining whether a child is related by legitimate kinship under Section 3(1)(j) of the Hindu Succession Act.

The Hindu Succession Act’s rules of devolution and distribution must be harmonized with the limitation in Section 16(3) of the Hindu Marriage Act that restricts the child’s property rights to the parents’ property.
